hero.title: Bjarnoy
hero.tagline: One island. One sea. Never at rest.
hero.pitch: Sail out, claim a plot, and build a realm that keeps growing while you're offline — build queues run, fleets sail, and raids land on a wall clock, not a turn counter.

oneView.title: One view — map and village
oneView.body: The world map and your village are the same hex lattice, not two screens. Zoom in on an island and the same rendered surface turns from territory and terrain into huts, farms and people — nothing ever "opens" a separate view.

features.title: Built to play, not just to look at
features.intro: Every feature below runs on the same engine you're looking at above — no mockups.

sharedIslands.title: Shared islands
sharedIslands.body: Islands are shared ground — many players' settlements can stand on the same island, side by side.

borders.title: Borders that grow
borders.body: Territory follows Settlers-II logic: your claim radius grows with your Longhouse and border towers, and contracts if they fall.

realTime.title: Real time, always running
realTime.body: Build queues, upgrades and fleets run on a wall clock. Log back in tomorrow and the world moved without you.

fogOfWar.title: Fog of war & scouting
fogOfWar.body: Unexplored ground stays hidden until a scout or a settlement reveals it — knowing the map is part of the game.

expansion.title: Expansion by sea
expansion.body: Load a settler crew onto a longship, sail it to an unclaimed coastal hex on any island, and found a second settlement.

trade.title: Trade between players
trade.body: Nothing is pooled — caravans and ships move goods between settlements, yours and anyone else's you strike a deal with.

guilds.title: Guilds & alliances
guilds.body: Band together with other jarls to share vision, coordinate landings, and hold islands jointly.

battles.title: Battles, reports & a simulator
battles.body: Raids and sieges resolve into readable battle reports, and a fight simulator lets you plan an attack before you commit troops.

engineering.title: Under the hood
engineering.intro: The portfolio half of this page — how it's actually built.

renderer.title: One hex renderer, two views
renderer.body: A single Pixi.js v8 renderer draws one axial hex lattice with an isometric projection — the world map and the village view are the same code path, just zoomed differently.

generation.title: Bit-exact island generation
generation.body: Procedural island shapes are generated identically on the .NET backend and in this TypeScript client, guarded by shared golden-fixture parity tests so the two never drift apart.

backend.title: .NET 10 + Aspire + PostgreSQL
backend.body: An ASP.NET Core backend orchestrated with .NET Aspire, backed by PostgreSQL, shipped as a single Docker image with this frontend built right in.

e2e.title: Sharded Playwright e2e suite
e2e.body: A real end-to-end test suite drives an actual browser against a production build, split across CI shards to keep runs fast.

deploy.title: Per-PR preview environments
deploy.body: Every pull request gets its own throwaway preview deployment on Coolify, so a change can be reviewed running, not just read as a diff.

i18n.title: English + German, fully in step
i18n.body: Every user-visible string ships in English and German, with automated tests enforcing key parity between the two.
